digest.en: Taiwan’s chip theft warnings and the pre-APEC US ban on Chinese genomic firms mark a widening biotech decoupling. Meanwhile, Rubio hosts a fractured G20 where Iran and Ukraine wars split the room.
digest.hi: बांग्लादेश में शेख हसीना के समर्थक को मौत की सजा सुनाई गई। इसी बीच ईरान और अमेरिका के बीच चार दिन की अंतिम मुदत का दबाव बढ़ रहा है।

articles.title: What Taiwan can teach South Korea about China’s chip tech theft
articles.summary: Three South Korean engineers allegedly stole proprietary probe-card designs for a Chinese employer. They used a local firm to modify the technology. The case highlights how talent migration facilitates industrial espionage. China now produces competing components. In November 2023, three engineers left a South Korean semiconductor testing-components company for a Chinese employer offering twice their previous salaries. According to South Korea’s Intellectual Property Office, they allegedly took proprietary probe-card designs, arranged for a Korean design firm to modify them, and used the technology to develop products in China.

articles.title: China ruling party says it 'eliminated dangers' after 33 expelled
articles.summary: Xi Jinping announced the expulsion of thirty-three Central Committee members. This follows his long-running anti-corruption campaign. The purge removed dozens of officials and military leaders. The ruling party claims these actions eliminated internal dangers. In more than a decade in charge, President Xi Jinping has cracked down hard on graft, ensnaring thousands of officials and purging dozens of members of the powerful Central Committee and a string of top military brass.

articles.title: Marco Rubio hosts G20 Foreign Ministers as Iran, Ukraine wars divide members
articles.summary: Marco Rubio hosted G20 foreign ministers in Atlanta. The meeting focused on energy and supply chain challenges. Members remain divided over the wars in Iran and Ukraine. The summit aimed to address geopolitical impacts on economic security. “Conversations in Atlanta will provide an opportunity to discuss energy and supply chain challenges as well as identify ways to collectively address the impact of geopolitical tensions on economic security,” a U. S.

articles.title: North Korea's Kim calls for rapid expansion of drone technology, observes testing of weapons
articles.summary: Kim Jong Un called for rapid expansion of North Korean drone technology. He observed weapons testing at a recent exhibition. The leader demanded absolute superiority in unmanned aeronautics. He announced unspecified steps to strengthen the sector. In a speech at the exhibition, Mr. Kim stressed the need to seize “the absolute superiority in the drone technology” and announced unspecified steps needed to “rapidly expand and strengthen the unmanned aeronautical technology,” says Korean Central News Agency.

articles.title: Republicans defend their bastions, as senate comes within reach of Democrats
articles.summary: Republicans hold a 53 to 47 Senate majority with 35 seats up for grabs. Seven are toss-ups in Iowa, Arkansas, Kansas, Maine, Michigan, Ohio, and Texas. All but Michigan are currently held by Republicans. Democrats are closing in on a potential majority shift. The GOP has a 53–47 majority in the Senate currently, with 35 seats being contested this year.

articles.title: The rise of the nuclear hexagon and the future of Asian stability
articles.summary: US nuclear strategy remains fragmented, prioritizing the US-Russia-China triangle while treating the China-India-Pakistan dynamic as a secondary regional issue. This oversight complicates stability in Asia, where nuclear postures are shifting. Washington’s focus on the northern axis leaves gaps in understanding southern Asian deterrence. The article argues that a cohesive approach is needed to address the evolving nuclear hexagon. Originally published by Pacific Forum, this article is republished with permission.

articles.title: Pre-APEC US ban on Chinese genomic giant widens biotech decoupling
articles.summary: Washington added three Shenzhen-based firms to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act list. The move blocks imports from China's leading genomics group. This extends the trade war into biotechnology. The ban arrived weeks before US and Chinese leaders meet in Shenzhen. Beijing has vowed to defend its firms after Washington blocked imports from China’s leading genomics group, extending the two countries’ trade war into biotechnology weeks before their leaders are due to meet in Shenzhen.

articles.title: 'A Reasonable Price': Inside Iran's Illicit Trade In Babies
articles.summary: Intermediaries on Iranian Telegram channels sell newborns for up to $1,100. They market the transactions as charitable acts. Some falsify birth records to hide the sales. Others arrange placements with Iranian families living abroad. This occurs despite a national ban on selling babies. Intermediaries on Iranian Telegram channels are offering newborns for up to $1,100 under the guise of charity, with some promising to falsify birth records and others arranging placements with Iranian families abroad, despite a ban on the sale of babies.

articles.title: The US Once Called It 'A Slush Fund For Putin.' Now Washington May Lift Sanctions On It
articles.summary: Washington is considering lifting sanctions on the Russian Direct Investment Fund. The fund's chief serves as the Kremlin's main negotiator with the White House. This move aims to normalize US-Russian ties. It also supports ongoing efforts to end the Ukraine war. Amid the swirl of efforts to end to the Ukraine war and normalize US-Russian ties, one idea under consideration: lifting sanctions on a massive Russian investment fund, whose chief is the Kremlin’s main go-between with White House negotiators.

articles.title: Moldovan President Calls Security Meeting After Massive Data Breach
articles.summary: Moldovan President Maia Sandu convened a national security meeting after a cyberattack exposed data for 750,000 people. Authorities are investigating possible foreign involvement. The attack may have utilized artificial intelligence tools to scale the breach across government systems. Moldovan President Maia Sandu has called a national security meeting after a major cyberattack exposed personal data linked to some 750,000 people.

articles.title: Esports is now geopolitics by other means
articles.summary: The competitive gaming industry has expanded into a global phenomenon. Over three million fans attended the 2025 Esports World Cup in Saudi Arabia. The event highlights how digital entertainment now intersects with international geopolitical influence and soft power. The competitive gaming industry has grown rapidly over the past two decades, transforming from a niche subculture into a global phenomenon watched by millions of spectators worldwide.

articles.title: AI is changing the way we think. The question is whether we’ll notice in time
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence now writes emails and summarizes reports in seconds. Many users view this capability as a major technological leap. The shift is comparable to the arrival of the internet. The rapid adoption raises questions about how people process information. Artificial intelligence promises to make life easier. With a few keystrokes, it can write emails, summarize reports, generate ideas and answer complex questions in seconds.

articles.title: Can new technology keep the world’s sea lanes safe?
articles.summary: The UN Security Council debated how cheap drones, autonomous vessels, and cyberattacks threaten global shipping. Delegates examined how these emerging technologies endanger seafarers and supply chains. They also discussed tools to protect trade and energy flows. Cheap drones, autonomous vessels and cyberattacks are changing the threats to the world’s shipping lanes – and the tools to counter them. At an open debate on Thursday, the Security Council is weighing how emerging technologies could both endanger and protect seafarers, global trade and food and energy supplies.

articles.title: Russian Drone Attack Kills 14 In Dnipro As Oleshky Truce Enters Third Day
articles.summary: The fragile cease-fire around Russian-occupied Oleshky reached its third day on October 29. Civilians face severe shortages and dangerous escape routes. Fears persist that Russia may use the pause to forcibly transfer residents to occupied Crimea. A fragile cease-fire around Russian-occupied Oleshky entered its third day on October 29, offering hope to thousands of civilians facing severe shortages and perilous escape routes, amid fears that Russia could use the pause to forcibly transfer residents to Russia or occupied Crimea.

articles.title: US ambassador suggests Trump could blame Canada if midterms don’t go his way
articles.summary: US ambassador Pete Hoekstra suggested Canada might face blame if Republicans lose next week's midterms. He previously accused Canadian officials of interfering in American elections. His comments have intensified a bitter dispute between the two nations. Pete Hoekstra, controversial US ambassador to Canada, has also accused Canadian officials of interfering in US electionsThe US ambassador has suggested Canada could be blamed if Republicans perform poorly in next week’s midterm elections, the latest intervention from a controversial figure who has been accused of inflaming a bitter dispute that has angered and baffled residents of both countries. O.

articles.title: The Mecca pact goes to Tehran. Can it keep the region out of another war?
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey sent senior officials to Tehran to negotiate with Iran under the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement. Prince Khalid bin Salman, Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Ibrahim Kalın met President Pezeshkian and security chief Mohsen Rezaei. The unusual diplomatic move aims to prevent regional escalation through direct dialogue. On Monday, the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement did something a defense treaty is not usually built to do.

articles.title: Civilians in Sudan’s El Obeid trapped between drones and incarceration
articles.summary: UN investigators reported that El Obeid civilians face drone strikes from the Rapid Support Forces. They also endure arbitrary arrests by the Sudanese Armed Forces. Residents live in constant fear of both military threats and state detention. Civilians in Sudan’s El Obeid live in constant fear of drone attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and of a wave of arbitrary arrests by the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), UN-appointed independent investigators said on Wednesday.

articles.title: UN human rights chief urges better protection of civilians in conflicts
articles.summary: Volker Türk highlighted youth-led protests in Serbia, Bangladesh, Nepal, and Madagascar. He noted these movements demand stronger human rights protections. The UN chief urged better civilian safeguards during conflicts. Youth-led protests against corruption and inequality in Serbia, Bangladesh, Nepal and Madagascar reflect a growing demand for reinforcing human rights around the world, UN human rights chief Volker Türk said at a press briefing on Wednesday.

articles.title: Ending conflict is ‘number one thing’ to reduce world hunger, new WFP chief says
articles.summary: Luke Lindberg, the new head of the UN World Food Programme, stated that ending conflict is the primary solution to global hunger. He noted that war drives two thirds of acute food insecurity affecting 266 million people worldwide. Lindberg emphasized that peace is the most effective tool for reducing starvation. Reducing conflict is the single most effective way to tackle global hunger, the new head of the UN World Food Programme (WFP), Luke Lindberg, said on Wednesday, noting that conflict drives two thirds of the acute food insecurity affecting 266 million people worldwide.

articles.title: Why Russia's Central Crimean Drone Base Is Hard For Ukraine To Destroy
articles.summary: Satellite imagery reveals a military airfield in central Crimea now functions as a primary hub for Russian drone launches. A Crimean military insider told RFE/RL that the site’s dispersed layout makes it difficult for Ukrainian forces to target effectively. The base uses multiple, smaller launch pads rather than a single concentrated runway. This fragmentation reduces the impact of any single precision strike. Ukraine has struggled to neutralize the facility despite repeated attempts. The infrastructure remains operational and continues to support Russian drone operations against Ukrainian targets.

articles.title: 'Committed To European Integration': Student List's Srdanovic On Serbia's Post-Vucic Future
articles.summary: Ilija Srdanovic, the lead candidate for Serbia’s Student List, confirmed the party’s commitment to European integration following Aleksandar Vucic’s defeat. The student-led opposition movement secured victory, ending over a decade of Vucic’s political dominance. Srdanovic outlined the next steps for the country in an interview with RFE/RL’s Balkan Service. The transition marks a significant shift in Serbian political leadership. Aleksandar Vucic’s election defeat has ended more than a decade of political dominance and handed victory to Serbia’s student-led opposition movement.

articles.title: Serbia Student List Lead Candidate Vows EU Integration, Open Debate On Russia Ties
articles.summary: Ilija Srdanovic leads Serbia's Student List party. The group recently ousted Aleksandar Vucic in elections. Srdanovic pledged to pursue EU integration. He also proposed a public debate on reconsidering sanctions against Russia. In an interview with RFE/RL, Ilija Srdanovic, the lead candidate for Serbia's Student List -- which ousted longtime leader Aleksandar Vucic in recent elections -- pledged to pursue EU integration and said Belgrade's stance on sanctions against Russia could be reconsidered through public debate.

articles.title: Will Trump Help Putin Win in Ukraine?
articles.summary: Crisis Group experts discussed the widening rift between Washington and Kyiv. They analyzed Russia’s intensifying attacks on Ukraine. European capitals are working to strengthen support while facing their own pressures. This week on Hold Your Fire!, Richard speaks with Crisis Group experts Lucian Kim, Stephen Pomper and Fabienne Hara about the latest rift between Washington and Kyiv, Russia’s intensifying attacks and European capitals’ efforts to strengthen Ukraine while themselves under pressure.

articles.title: How Algeria’s Rupture with the UAE Could Roil the Region
articles.summary: Algeria severed diplomatic ties with the United Arab Emirates. The split follows years of discord over North Africa and the Sahel. Both nations view the dispute differently. The rivalry now threatens broader regional stability. Algiers has severed diplomatic ties with Abu Dhabi, following years of discord over crises in North Africa and the Sahel. The two countries see their dispute very differently, but it has nonetheless become a rivalry that could put regional stability at risk.

articles.title: A Trigger in Jammu and Kashmir: Militant Violence under Indian Central Rule
articles.summary: India revoked Jammu and Kashmir's special status in August 2019, replacing its autonomous arrangement with direct central rule. The move reduced some militant activity but sparked new protests and political backlash. New Delhi now faces pressure to revise its approach to restore stability. In 2019, India made far-reaching changes to governance in Jammu and Kashmir, with the aim of quelling insurgency.

articles.summary: हैरी पॉटर सीरीज इस साल क्रिसमस पर रिलीज होगी। मेकर्स ने आधिकारिक तौर पर तारीख की घोषणा कर दी है। फैंस ने हॉगवर्ट्स के नए लुक पर अपनी प्रतिक्रिया देना शुरू कर दिया है। Harry Potter: सीरीज हैरी पॉटर को लेकर फैंस काफी उत्साहित हैं। इस बीच मेकर्स ने इसकी रिलीज डेट का एलान कर दिया है। यह सीरीज इस साल क्रिसमस के मौके पर रिलीज होने वाली है।

articles.title: 'बहुत खराब दिखते हो', पत्रकार ने किया सवाल तो भड़के ट्रंप, सेहत सुधारने की दी सलाह
articles.summary: डोनाल्ड ट्रंप ने सेहत के सवाल पर पत्रकार को फिटनेस सुधारने की सलाह दी। उन्होंने कंसास और आयोवा की चुनावी रैलियाँ रद्द कर दी थीं। अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रंप एक पत्रकार पर भड़क गए हैं. एक पत्रकार के ट्रंप से उनकी सेहत के बारे में पूछे जाने पर उन्हें गुस्सा आ गया. उन्होंने उसके लुक्स पर टिप्पणी कर दी. ट्रंप ने कहा, पहले अपनी फिटनेस सुधारो.
